findings.issue_text: [High/bug] `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` raises KeyError (HTTP 500) when existing Integration metadata lacks a `sender` key, breaking reinstallation of legacy/deactivated integrations; use `.get()` with fail-closed handling

[Medium/security] The `except Integration.DoesNotExist: return pipeline.next_step()` path skips installer-identity verification entirely, allowing a user to link an installation with no verification if the `installation.created` webhook hasn't been processed yet (race window)

[Medium/security] OAuth `state` is `pipeline.signature`, which is deterministic rather than session-bound/random (tests hardcode identical state across flows with different users/orgs), defeating the CSRF check; use a cryptographically random per-pipeline nonce persisted in pipeline state

[Medium/bug] `safe_urlopen(...)` token exchange and `get_user_info(...)` are outside any try/except, causing unhandled 500s on network errors; additionally the bare `except Exception: payload = {}` around `safe_urlread`/`parse_qsl` silently swallows all errors with no logging/metrics

[Medium/test_gap] test_installation_not_found posts state `ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05` which differs from the signature every other flow produces, so the assertion passes via the state-mismatch branch of `error()` rather than the intended `Integration.DoesNotExist` path — the test doesn't exercise what its name claims

[Medium/test_gap] No test coverage for the new failure modes: OAuth callback with missing/invalid `state`, user denying authorization (`code` absent), token exchange returning no `access_token`, and `get_user_info` failing

[Low/bug] The authorize redirect is built with an f-string and no URL-encoding: `f"...&redirect_uri={redirect_uri}"`, which breaks if `redirect_uri` contains `&` or `=`; params should be assembled with `urlencode`

[Low/data] The sender comparison `fetch_state("github_authenticated_user") != integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` is case-sensitive, but GitHub logins are case-insensitive, producing false "Invalid installation request" errors; compare case-insensitively

[Low/bug] The token response is parsed assuming a form-encoded body via `dict(parse_qsl(body))`, but GitHub returns JSON if the request carries `Accept: application/json`, in which case every install would fail; parse defensively (try JSON, fall back to form-encoding)

[Low/bug] `request.GET.get("installation_id", pipeline.fetch_state("installation_id"))` in GitHubInstallation.dispatch lets a GET parameter override the pipeline-bound installation_id and re-bind it, allowing the query parameter to fully control which installation gets linked without identity verification; prefer trusting the pipeline-bound value or re-verifying consistency

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/security] The `except Integration.DoesNotExist: return pipeline.next_step()` path skips installer-identity verification entirely, allowing a user to link an installation with no verification if the `installation.created` webhook hasn't been processed yet (race window)

adjudication.rationale: In `GitHubInstallation.dispatch`, the installer-identity check (`pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user") != integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]`) is only executed in the branch where an ACTIVE `Integration` already exists. If `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)` raises `Integration.DoesNotExist`, the code immediately `return pipeline.next_step()` (after binding `installation_id`), which means the flow proceeds without any identity verification. Given the verification relies on `integration.metadata["sender"]` (apparently populated by the installation webhook), this creates exactly the described race window: if the webhook hasn’t created/populated the Integration yet, the new verification is skipped entirely.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] `safe_urlopen(...)` token exchange and `get_user_info(...)` are outside any try/except, causing unhandled 500s on network errors; additionally the bare `except Exception: payload = {}` around `safe_urlread`/`parse_qsl` silently swallows all errors with no logging/metrics

adjudication.rationale: In `OAuthLoginView.dispatch`, the OAuth token exchange call `req = safe_urlopen(...)` is executed outside any `try/except` (new code around `# similar to OAuth2CallbackView.exchange_token`). If `safe_urlopen` raises (e.g., network/timeout/SSL), the request will bubble up as an unhandled exception (500) rather than returning the integration error page like other failure paths. Similarly, `authenticated_user_info = get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` is not guarded; if it raises on request/parse failures, it can also 500. Additionally, the `except Exception: payload = {}` around `safe_urlread(req).decode(...)` / `parse_qsl` swallows all exceptions with no logging/metrics, making failures silent and harder to debug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] test_installation_not_found posts state `ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05` which differs from the signature every other flow produces, so the assertion passes via the state-mismatch branch of `error()` rather than the intended `Integration.DoesNotExist` path — the test doesn't exercise what its name claims

adjudication.rationale: Verified: `OAuthLoginView.dispatch` returns `error()` when `request.GET['state'] != pipeline.signature`. In `test_installation_not_found`, the second GET uses `state=ddd023d87a...`, while other flows in this diff assert the pipeline signature/state is `9cae5e...` (see `assert_setup_flow` redirect assertion). Therefore the test’s `Invalid installation request.` assertion is satisfied via the state-mismatch branch, and it does not exercise the intended `Integration.DoesNotExist`/"installation not found" behavior implied by the test name.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] No test coverage for the new failure modes: OAuth callback with missing/invalid `state`, user denying authorization (`code` absent), token exchange returning no `access_token`, and `get_user_info` failing

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new OAuth callback/error branches in `OAuthLoginView.dispatch`: invalid/missing `state` compared to `pipeline.signature` returns `error(...)`; missing `code` leads to token exchange with `code=None` and then `if "access_token" not in payload: return error(...)`; parsing failures set `payload = {}`; and `get_user_info(...)` without a `login` returns `error(...)`. The updated tests cover the happy path OAuth redirect/callback and one invalid-state case (`test_installation_not_found` now asserts `Invalid installation request.`), plus a user mismatch case. But there is no explicit test for the callback when the user denies authorization / `code` is absent, when the token endpoint returns no `access_token`, or when `get_user_info` fails/returns no `login` (those paths are new and untested).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] The authorize redirect is built with an f-string and no URL-encoding: `f"...&redirect_uri={redirect_uri}"`, which breaks if `redirect_uri` contains `&` or `=`; params should be assembled with `urlencode`

adjudication.rationale: The diff does build the authorize URL via an f-string: `...&redirect_uri={redirect_uri}` in `OAuthLoginView.dispatch`. However, in this code path `redirect_uri` is constructed as `absolute_uri(reverse(...))`, which (as shown) is a fixed path with no querystring, so it will not contain `&` or `=` that would “break” the URL. The finding asserts a concrete breakage scenario that isn’t supported by what the diff shows; at most this is a general robustness/style improvement to use `urlencode`, not a verifiable defect here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/data] The sender comparison `fetch_state("github_authenticated_user") != integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` is case-sensitive, but GitHub logins are case-insensitive, producing false "Invalid installation request" errors; compare case-insensitively

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a strict string inequality check `pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user") != integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` in `GitHubInstallation.dispatch`. This comparison is case-sensitive as written, so if the two sources ever differ only by casing it will trigger the generic `error()` path (“Invalid installation request”). The diff itself doesn’t establish whether GitHub guarantees consistent casing between `/user` and webhook `sender.login`, so the “will produce false errors” aspect isn’t fully verifiable from the diff, but normalizing case would make the new validation more robust.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] The token response is parsed assuming a form-encoded body via `dict(parse_qsl(body))`, but GitHub returns JSON if the request carries `Accept: application/json`, in which case every install would fail; parse defensively (try JSON, fall back to form-encoding)

adjudication.rationale: In OAuthLoginView the token exchange uses `safe_urlopen(..., data=data)` and then parses the response with `dict(parse_qsl(body))`. The diff does not show any `Accept: application/json` header being sent (nor any other indication the request asks for JSON), and the added tests stub a form-encoded body (`body='access_token=...'`) consistent with GitHub’s default behavior when `Accept` is not set. Therefore the claim that GitHub will return JSON and “every install would fail” is not verifiable from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] `request.GET.get("installation_id", pipeline.fetch_state("installation_id"))` in GitHubInstallation.dispatch lets a GET parameter override the pipeline-bound installation_id and re-bind it, allowing the query parameter to fully control which installation gets linked without identity verification; prefer trusting the pipeline-bound value or re-verifying consistency

adjudication.rationale: In `GitHubInstallation.dispatch`, `installation_id` is chosen via `request.GET.get("installation_id", pipeline.fetch_state("installation_id"))`, so if a pipeline already has a bound `installation_id`, a subsequent request can override it by supplying a different `installation_id` query param, and the code immediately re-binds it (`pipeline.bind_state("installation_id", installation_id)`). The added identity check (`github_authenticated_user` vs `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]`) only runs in the branch where an ACTIVE `Integration` already exists; if `Integration.DoesNotExist` it proceeds (`return pipeline.next_step()`) without any such consistency/identity validation in this diff. This makes the finding’s concern (GET parameter controls the installation id even when pipeline state exists) verifiable and potentially security-relevant.
